Here is a consolidated, clear summary of the full 12-week upper-body strength program for your client, integrated with cardio, hangboard, climbing prep, mobility, and the new Saturday Finisher Day. It’s organized by phase, week, and session type, with recommended loads, rep ranges, and key coaching notes. Also included are nutrition, recovery, and safety reminders to keep everything coherent and easy to hand to the client.

Overall goals
- Build upper-body strength and shoulder health for a recreational climber with right subacromial impingement.
- Maintain pain-free ROM and scapular control; progressively load within safe ranges.
- Recompose body with a focus on lean mass gains while supporting climbing endurance and technique.
- Reintroduce longer climbing days with appropriate conditioning, grip work, and climbing-specific prep.
- Add two cardio sessions per week to support endurance and long climbing days.
- Add a Saturday Finisher Day for weekly general fitness and mobility play.
- Week 9–12 include hangboard and climbing-specific prep, culminating in a peak in Week 12 for a climbing trip.

Program structure at a glance
- Training days: 3 upper-body strength sessions per week (A, B, C), non-consecutive (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Cardio days: 2 per week (D1, D2), non-consecutive from lifting days. Hangboard and climbing prep concentrated in Weeks 9–12.
- Mobility: integrated daily mobility routine (8–12 minutes) focusing on thoracic mobility, scapular control, cuff health, and hip/ankle mobility. Included in warm-ups and as a daily habit.
- Saturday Finisher Day: 60-minute full-body, low-to-moderate intensity finisher session on Saturdays. Optional depending on climbing load and fatigue.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundation, mobility, scapular control
Goals: establish pain-free ROM, scapular awareness, rotator cuff endurance, technique, and low-load upper-body exposure.

Weekly structure
- Week 1–4: 3 upper-body sessions (A, B, C) with conservative ROM and loads. 0–1 cardio days integrated per week initially (progressing to 1 cardio day as tolerance allows). Mobility daily.

Sample sessions (A, B, C) — foundational templates
- Session A: 
  - Lower-body work optional (Goblet squat 3x8)
  - Floor press neutral grip 3x12
  - Cable low row 3x12
  - Dumbbell lateral raise to 90° 3x12
  - External rotation 0–15° 3x15
  - Scapular push-ups 3x12
  - Farmer’s carry light 2x30m
- Session B:
  - Anti-rotation band work 3x15
  - Seated cable row 3x12
  - Incline press with limited ROM 3x10
  - Prone Y raises 3x12
  - Prone external rotation 0–20° 3x12
  - Pallof press 3x12 per side
- Session C:
  - Neutral grip DB bench 3x12
  - Lat pulldown neutral grip 3x12
  - Face pulls 3x15
  - External rotation at side 3x15
  - Hanging scapular retractions 3x30s
  - Core anti-rotation dead bug 3x10 per side

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — Capacity and integration
Goals: increase loading within safe ROM, add climbing-specific stabilization, more vertical pulling and pressing within ROM, mild incline pressing; continue scapular and cuff work; build overall work capacity.

Weekly structure
- 3 upper-body sessions (A, B, C) with increased volume and slightly higher loads.
- Cardio: 2x per week, Zone 2, 30–45 minutes per session (progressing after Week 4).
- Mobility remains a daily focus; climbing drills introduced as tolerated.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 — Strength and transfer; peak for climbing trip in Week 12
Goals: higher-intensity, speed-oriented strength block within safe ROM; climbing-transfer work with grip and core conditioning; hangboard and climbing prep begin Week 9, culminating in a taper Week 12.

Weekly structure
- 3 upper-body strength sessions (A, B, C) with higher velocity work and controlled ROM to maximize rate of force development, while protecting the shoulder.
- Cardio: 2 days/week Zone 2; optional short intervals if recovery allows (only if shoulder remains pain-free and climbing performance is not compromised).
- Hangboard and climbing prep: Weeks 9–12, non-overhead grips, scapular control, and finger tendon conditioning; progressive volume but with strict pain-free rules.
- Climbing prep: technique and endurance focus with low to moderate loads; avoid heavy lock-offs.
- Saturday Finisher Day: optional weekend full-body finisher that promotes movement quality and mobility.

Session specifics for Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12)
- Week 9
  - A: Floor press 5x5 tempo 2-0-1-0; Seated row 4x8; Lateral raises 3x12; Pallof press 3x12; Farmer’s carry 2x100m; Prone Y raises 3x12
  - B: Incline press 5x5 0–30°; Wide-grip pull-down 4x8; External rotation 0–15° 3x12; Face pulls 4x15; Core anti-rotation 3x12
  - C: Neutral DB press 5x5; Lat pull-down 4x8; Scapular stability 3x12; Prone external rotation 3x12; Anti-extension core circuit 3 rounds
  - Cardio: 2x Zone 2; one short optional interval
  - Hangboard: 6–8 sets 8–10s on large edge; optional 1–2 sets 4–6s half-crimp if tolerated
  - Climbing prep: 1 technique-focused session (30–45 min)
- Week 10
  - A: Floor press 5x5 tempo; Seated row 4x8; Lateral raises 3x12; Pallof press 3x12; Farmer’s carry 2x110m
  - B: Incline press 5x5; Cable low row 4x8; Face pulls 4x15; Core anti-rotation 3x12; Grip endurance set optional
  - C: Neutral DB press 5x5; Lat pull-down 4x8; Scapular stability 3x15; External rotation 3x12; Grip/anti-slip work 2x30–45s
  - Cardio: 2 days; one longer steady-state, one light interval optional
  - Hangboard: 7–8 sets 6–8s; optional 1 set 4–6s
  - Climbing prep: technique + light endurance boulder
- Week 11
  - A: Floor press 4x4; Seated row 4x6–8; Lateral raises 3x12; Pallof press 3x12; Farmer’s carry 2x120m
  - B: Incline press 4x4; Wide-grip pull-down 4x6–8; External rotation 3x12; Face pulls 4x15; Core anti-rotation 3x12
  - C: Neutral DB press 4x4; Lat pull-down 4x6–8; Scapular stability 3x12; External rotation 3x12; Grip carries 2x30–45s
  - Climbing prep: moderate-intensity climb stress; avoid high-load lock-offs
  - Hangboard: maintain 6–8s sets if tolerated
- Week 12 (taper and peak)
  - A: Floor press 3x6; Seated row 3x8; Lateral raises 3x12; Pallof press 3x12; Farmer’s carry 2x90m
  - B: Incline press 3x6; Wide-grip pull-down 3x8; External rotation 3x12; Face pulls 3x12; Core anti-rotation 3x12
  - C: Neutral DB press 3x6; Lat pull-down 3x8; Scapular mobility sequence 3x12; External rotation 3x12; Grip/anti-slip 2x30–45s
  - Climbing prep: short, technique-focused climbs; posture, rhythm, and breathing
  - Hangboard: deloaded 4–6 sets 6–8s on large edges; no new grip experiments
  - Cardio: maintain 2 days but lower volume for fresh shoulders and legs
  - Saturday Finisher Day: optional but recommended to maintain movement quality

Mobility plan (embedded)
- Daily 8–12 minute mobility routine, focusing on:
  - Thoracic spine extension, rib-cage expansion, and breathing
  - Scapular mobility and scapular plane ROM
  - Rotator cuff and posterior cuff mobility
  - Lat stretch and thoracic breathing integration
  - Hip and ankle mobility for climbing position maintenance
- Phase-specific emphasis:
  - Phase 1: foundational ROM, pain-free ranges
  - Phase 2: thoracic extension, scapular control, and climbing drill integration
  - Phase 3: priority on thoracic mobility before heavy loading and climbing prep days
- Warm-up integration: include 2–3 mobility drills in the warm-up for shoulder health on every lifting day

Hangboard and climbing-specific prep (Weeks 9–12)
- Hangboard: start with large-edge, pain-free hangs; gradual progression to mid-to-large edges only if tolerance remains.
- Climbing-specific drills: focus on technique, footwork, body positioning, and endurance rather than maximum grip strength. Keep sessions pain-free and within ROM.
- Campus-style and controlled bouldering: only if shoulder is pain-free and technique-focused, with proper rest and lower loads.

Saturday Finisher Day (new addition)
- 60-minute full-body, fun finisher after main session or on separate weekend day
- 4 stations (60 seconds each with 20 seconds rest), 4 rounds in Circuit A; 4 rounds in Circuit B (shorter), plus a 6–8 minute finisher burst and mobility cooldown
- Emphasize non-overhead movements, grip endurance, core stability, and mobility
- Optional variations: partner workout or playful competition to boost adherence

Nutrition and recovery (as previously outlined)
- Daily protein: 1.9–2.3 g/kg
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg baseline; higher around training and long climbing days
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; electrolytes as needed
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day; vitamin D3 if deficient; omega-3s; caffeine 3–6 mg/kg pre-workout as tolerated
- Weekly adjustment: track body weight, strength progress, energy, and climbing performance; adjust calories by 100–200 kcal as needed

Progression rules and safety
- Progression is load-based: increase load when all sets/reps are completed with clean technique and no pain.
- Pain guidance: any new pain or increased impingement symptoms require regression to previous ROM and loads; consult physio if persistent.
- Shoulder health first: scapular control and thoracic mobility must be solid before heavy loading or high-intensity climbing-specific work.
- Climbing days: if fatigue or pain emerges, scale back climbs or reduce subsequent loading.

Customization options
- If you want, I can convert this into:
  - A precise week-by-week schedule with exact numbers for your client’s actual current strength baselines (e.g., 1RM equivalents or estimated working weights).
  - A printable calendar with A/B/C daily plans, cardio days, hangboard days, mobility, and Sunday rest.
  - A version tailored to available equipment (e.g., substitutions for incline bench, specific machines, or alternate grips).

Would you like me to generate a fully detailed, week-by-week printable plan with exact sets/reps/rests for Weeks 1–12 aligned to your preferred workout order (A/B/C) and the client’s exact strength baselines? If you provide the client’s current 1RM estimates or recent working sets, I can tailor precise loading and progression.
